source: original; stimulus from the shared image pool or paraphrased from the grounding books
stem: Which of the following best describes what the INF Treaty did?

options.text: It ended the Soviet war in Afghanistan and withdrew Soviet troops
options.misconception: The Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan came in 1989 and was separate from the treaty.

options.text: It created the Strategic Defense Initiative
options.misconception: SDI was an American research program announced in 1983, not created by the treaty.

options.text: It eliminated an entire class of intermediate-range missiles
It admitted the Soviet Union into NATO
options.misconception: The Soviet Union never joined NATO; the treaty was about missiles, not membership.

rationales.A: Afghanistan is not mentioned in the treaty. Background: Soviet troops left Afghanistan in 1989, two years after the treaty.
rationales.B: SDI predates the treaty by four years. Background: the Strategic Defense Initiative was Reagan's 1983 missile-defense research program.
rationales.C: The treaty required both sides to destroy their ground-launched missiles in the 500-to-5,500-kilometer range. Background: it was the first agreement to eliminate a whole class of nuclear weapons rather than merely limit them.
rationales.D: NATO membership was never part of the treaty. Background: the Soviet Union remained outside NATO until it dissolved in 1991.
rationales.general:
1. Read the treaty for its verbs: destroy, eliminate, verify.
2. The missiles it covers are ground-launched, with ranges between 500 and 5,500 kilometers.
3. Background: it was the first agreement to eliminate a whole class of nuclear weapons rather than merely limit them.
4. The other choices name real events, but none of them is what this treaty did.
Remember: the INF Treaty did not limit missiles, it removed a whole kind of them.

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the INF Treaty, December 8, 1987. Post-1929 material is paraphrased, not quoted.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty, signed in Washington on December 8, 1987: The United States and the Soviet Union agreed to destroy all of their ground-launched missiles with ranges between 500 and 5,500 kilometers. Inspectors from each side would visit the other's territory to verify that the missiles were destroyed.
